data.research_question: Which current or historically relevant public organizations, communication surfaces, and explicitly public organizational representatives can be verified in the next unresolved shard-C U.S. geographic NPAs 404, 407, and 410?
data.method: Bounded deterministic shard-C area-code enumeration using current U.S. geographic NPA references, literal and locality-derived public web searches, first-party/current-status verification, repository dedupe, historical-directory seed checking, and explicit-public-role person cross-enumeration.
classification_rules: Historical directories and stale first-party pages are discovery seeds only; current-status verification is required before calling an organization active.
Do not infer individual political affiliation from organizational proximity, attendance, volunteering, employment, or public representation.
Person↔org relations in this pass are recorded only when the role is explicitly stated in a public source; no inferred political-affiliation relations are created.
Do not merge organizations or people from name or handle similarity alone.

findings.notes: Atlanta Food Not Bombs and Atlanta Solidarity Fund are current; The Teardown Community remains a historically explicit anarchist/autonomous seed but was not promoted to active because visible first-party activity is stale. Atlanta Solidarity Fund public Bluesky handle @atlsolfund.bsky.social was captured.

Orlando Against Police Crimes and H3RD Collective are current/recent. Public reporting explicitly names Cassia Laham, Richard Thomas, and Edmund Anglero in OAPC organizer/emcee roles; these role records do not infer political affiliation.

Red Emma's is current and first-party history traces it to an anarchist collective bookstore; Baltimore Food Not Bombs has recent September 2026 partner/event corroboration. A current first-party Red Emma's bio explicitly identifies John Duda as a co-founder.
